question.text: In which decade will the 2026 UK Christmas number one have been originally released?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the decade of the original release of the 2026 [UK Christmas number one](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UK_singles_chart_Christmas_number_ones).
question.fine_print:
This question will resolve based on the release date of the specific recording that tops the charts. It is immaterial whether a different version of the single was recorded and released previously. 
For example in 2004, this question would have resolved as 2000s because that year's Christmas number one: Band Aid 20's version of "Do They Know It's Christmas?," was released in 2004, even though the original "Do They Know It's Christmas?" was recorded and released in 1984.
Each decade will be defined by the first three digits of the year. For example, any recording released between January 1, 1990, and December 31, 1999, will be considered a 1990s release.

I've finished the searches and am writing up the findings.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on the [Wikipedia list of UK Christmas number ones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UK_singles_chart_Christmas_number_ones), which follows the Official Charts Company. The latest entry is 2025: Kylie Minogue's "XMAS". The two years before were Wham!'s "Last Christmas" (1984) in 2023 and 2024. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UK_singles_chart_Christmas_number_ones)
- 2026 date: the Official Charts Company will announce the Christmas Number 1 on Friday 25 December 2026, on BBC Radio 1's Official Chart with Jack Saunders. [OfficialCharts](https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/when-will-the-christmas-number-1-2026-be-announced/)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing is settled yet. In practice it comes down to "Last Christmas" (1980s) against a 2020s release. Every other named contender is a 2020s recording.
- 2025-12-19: "XMAS" was named Christmas No. 1 and "Last Christmas" came second. [OfficialCharts](https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/christmas-number-1-2025-kylie-minogue-xmas/)
- "XMAS" came out digitally on 2025-11-05 as an Amazon exclusive, with CD and vinyl following on 2025-12-12. It sold 55,926 units in its first chart week. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XMAS_(song))

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-29 (week ending): Jamie Miller's "Babydoll" is listed at UK No. 1. Before it came Taylor Swift's "Patient Zero" (from 8 Oct, 3 weeks), Sienna Spiro's "Great Expectation" (from 17 Sep) and Ella Langley's "Choosin' Texas" (10 Sep). Sam Fender and Olivia Dean's "Rein Me In" was the year's dominant hit, with more than 20 weeks at No. 1 across several runs. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UK_singles_chart_number_ones_of_the_2020s)
- 2026-01-01 (week ending): "Last Christmas" returned to No. 1 in the week after Christmas 2025. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UK_singles_chart_number_ones_of_the_2020s)
- I found no announced 2026 charity or novelty Christmas single from LadBaby, Band Aid or Kylie, and no confirmed new Kylie Christmas release. [search results](https://www.olbg.com/news/christmas-number-one-2026-odds-wham-set-early-festive-pace)

## 4. Base rates
- 2023 to 2025: two of three Christmas No. 1s were 1980s recordings (Wham!) and one was a 2020s release.
- 2010 to 2022: every winner was released in its own decade. That covers the X Factor winners, the LadBaby run from 2018 to 2022 and Ed Sheeran's "Perfect" (2017). [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UK_singles_chart_Christmas_number_ones)
- Older catalogue winners are rare. From my own knowledge (not checked in this session): 1991, Queen's "Bohemian Rhapsody" reissue (1975 recording, so 1970s); 2009, Rage Against the Machine's "Killing in the Name" (1992, so 1990s). Mariah Carey's "All I Want for Christmas Is You" (1994) has never been UK Christmas No. 1, as far as I know.
- Trend: since streaming took over and the charity or novelty singles faded after LadBaby, the main fight is between "Last Christmas" and a strong current release, often one with physical formats. That is how Kylie won in 2025.

## 5. Other forecasts
- 2026-10-21 (OLBG, "theoretical" odds from an industry expert; their article says betting sites are not taking bets yet): Wham! 1/3 (75%); Sam Fender and Olivia Dean 6/4; Ella Langley 2/1; Olivia Rodrigo, Taylor Swift and Ed Sheeran 3/1 each; Kylie Minogue 4/1; Ashe 6/1; Sidemen 10/1; Bov Boys 12/1. The implied probabilities add up to well over 100%. Every option except Wham! would resolve 2020s. [OLBG](https://www.olbg.com/news/christmas-number-one-2026-odds-betting-experts-back-last-christmas-reclaim-christmas-number-one-spot)
- The Punter's Page has Wham! at 3/10, but the page may be out of date. [ThePuntersPage](https://www.thepunterspage.com/christmas-number-one-odds/)
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on the UK Christmas No. 1. The Kalshi markets supplied are about the US Billboard chart and do not match this question. One is only loosely relevant: "All I Want for Christmas Is You" ranked 1 to 2 on the Hot 100 for 26 Dec 2026 is priced at 0.85. That points to strong catalogue streaming for Christmas songs, but in the US.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- November to mid-December 2026: possible new Christmas singles or physical-format pushes (a Kylie follow-up, YouTuber or Sidemen novelty singles, charity singles), and the build-up of streams for catalogue Christmas songs.
- Mid-December: the Official Charts midweek updates for the Christmas chart week. In 2025 the midweek leader on 14 December went on to win.
- 2026-12-25: the Christmas No. 1 announcement. [OfficialCharts](https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/when-will-the-christmas-number-1-2026-be-announced/)

(b) **Status quo:** "Last Christmas" by Wham!, a 1984 recording, so 1980s. It was No. 1 at Christmas in 2023 and 2024, came second in 2025, and returned to No. 1 in the week after Christmas 2025. No charity single, novelty single or Kylie follow-up has been announced so far.

- In the streaming era without LadBaby, the contest is essentially Wham! against a strong current release that also sells physical formats.

(d) **Strongest evidence:**
- OLBG theoretical odds (21 October 2026) give Wham! 1/3, about 75% implied. The Punter's Page has 3/10. Every other named contender (Fender and Dean, Langley, Rodrigo, Swift, Sheeran, Kylie, Sidemen) would resolve 2020s.
- In 2026 the chart week ends on Christmas Eve, which is the peak for catalogue Christmas streaming. In 2025 the week ended on 18 December, which made it easier for Kylie's physical-format push to win. The 2026 calendar therefore favours Wham! more than 2025's did.
- No 2026 charity or novelty campaign has been confirmed as of late October.
- I found no liquid market on this exact question. The Kalshi markets supplied cover the US Billboard chart and are not a match.

(e) **Unexpected outcome scenario:**
- A Sidemen, YouTuber or charity single launched in December with heavy bundling of physical formats, or a surprise Taylor Swift or Kylie Christmas release, beats Wham!. That gives 2020s.
- Alternatively, Mariah overtakes Wham! in the streams for the week including Christmas Eve, giving 1990s.

**Reasoning:** I start from about 75% for Wham! based on the betting odds. I move slightly down, to 68%, to leave room for a late campaign by a current release, since that is what happened in 2025. The calendar effect offsets some of that move. Most of the rest goes to 2020s, with small amounts on Mariah (1990s), "Fairytale of New York" (1980s, already covered) and other catalogue tails.
